name: Blink input (webcam eyes and look-away)
what: Turns the webcam into a controller: eyes closed (both eyes to close, either eye to open, so squints and winks never count), looking away (head turned, face out of frame, tab hidden, each with a grace time so slow trackers don't flicker) and a coarse left/centre/right gaze, as clean events (blindStart/blindEnd, eyesClosed/eyesOpened, lookAwayStart/End). An 8-second calibration fits the thresholds to each player's own eyes. Falls back to holding Space or an on-screen button, with simulated blinks when there is no camera, and drops to that fallback if the camera dies mid-game. Includes a scripted synthetic face for bots and tests. MediaPipe runs locally; no video leaves the device.
use_when: the game is played with the player's eyes or face: blinking, closing the eyes, looking away from the screen or turning the head (for example 'it only moves when you can't see it').

third_party.what: MediaPipe Tasks Vision (npm dependency; wasm runtime copied into public/wasm at install)
third_party.author: Google

third_party.what: Face Landmarker model face_landmarker.task (downloaded at install, sha256-checked, not committed)
third_party.author: Google

good_for: Games built around 'can the player see the screen?': horror where things move while you blink, stealth with closed eyes, staring contests, meditation or rest timers, look-away pauses, head-turn choices. Any renderer.
not_for: Precise eye-gaze aiming (the gaze is three coarse zones); games that must work without a fallback; phones in poor light. Never verified with a real face by a person yet: plan a human test early.
how_to_add: node tools/blocks/add.mjs meticulai-blink-input, then in my-game: npm install @mediapipe/tasks-vision@1.1.0 and node vendor/meticulai-blink-input/scripts/fetch-model.mjs --out public (see HOW-TO-USE.md)
